title: Origins and Road to War
sub: How the Tajikistani Civil War began

slides.title: From Transnistria War to Tajikistani Civil War
slides.cap: Historical connection: Post-Soviet state collapse and factional conflict
slides.body: The Soviet collapse removed the institutions that had contained regional and ideological competition in Tajikistan. Rival factions then fought for control of the newly independent state.

stats.lbl: Post-Soviet state collapse and factional conflict
The Soviet collapse removed the institutions that had contained regional and ideological competition in Tajikistan. Rival factions then fought for control of the newly independent state.

slides.title: Before the Tajikistani Civil War
slides.body:
Political competition after Soviet collapse split Tajikistan among regional, former communist, democratic, and Islamist factions.

The Conflict Takes Shape: The war determined control of the new state and the political place of opposition movements and regional communities. The opening phase established the political goals, alliances, and military problems that shaped every later campaign.

stats.val: The war determined control of the new state and the political place of opposition movements and regional communities.

slides.title: Operation Hisar
slides.body:
Operation Hisar marked an important episode in the Tajikistani Civil War. It showed how the conflict's political goals were being translated into military action and placed new pressure on both the battlefield and surrounding communities.

Why This Moment Matters: Operation Hisar was more than an isolated engagement. It helped define the conflict's direction and exposed the strengths and weaknesses of the opposing sides. The war determined control of the new state and the political place of opposition movements and regional communities.

Consequences: The effects of Operation Hisar extended beyond its immediate result. Fighting, persecution, and economic collapse killed tens of thousands and displaced hundreds of thousands. Its place in the wider campaign also influenced later military choices and political calculations.

title: International and Human Dimensions
sub: The wider impact of the Tajikistani Civil War

slides.title: International Dimension
slides.body:
Russia and Uzbekistan backed the government, while opposition forces operated from Afghanistan and peace talks involved the UN and Iran.

The Human Cost: Fighting, persecution, and economic collapse killed tens of thousands and displaced hundreds of thousands.

title: Outcome and Legacy
sub: How the Tajikistani Civil War ended and what followed

slides.title: The End of the Tajikistani Civil War
slides.body: A 1997 peace agreement integrated parts of the opposition into government, though power later became increasingly centralized.
